tagline: From the artichoke town to Prunedale, whose plums died young.
intro: East of Castroville, Highway 156 comes down from freeway to a two-lane road for the four miles to US 101 at Prunedale. It is a heavily traveled stretch, part of the quickest way between the Bay Area and the Monterey Peninsula.

This was slough country once, crisscrossed by swamps. In the 1840s a mapmaker crossing near here wrote of a patch of turf where the ground trembled under the horses' feet. Castroville, at the west end, calls itself the Artichoke Center of the World and holds a festival to prove it.

moments.title: Castroville
moments.text: Juan Bautista Castro founded the town in 1863 on his family's rancho. To fill it, 100 lots were given away by lottery to anyone who would clear the land and build a house.

moments.title: Prunedale
moments.text: Named for a plum orchard that died early for want of irrigation and fertilizer. The name was kept.
